item.title: Wisbech fan pays tribute following death of Dolly Parton
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech fan pays tribute following death of Dolly Parton
A Wisbech man has shared his memories of meeting Dolly Parton following the news of the singer’s death this week at the age of 80. Michael Creed, a long-time admirer of the American star, first met her backstage at London’s Hammersmith Apollo in 2002. Mr. Creed, who co-founded a UK fan newsletter in the late 1990s, later met the icon again during a television appearance. He described the singer as a down-to-earth person who made time for her supporters. Mr. Creed, who has collected extensive memorabilia of the artist since 1974, said he was in shock following the announcement of her passing.

item.title: King’s Lynn charity secures funding to support veterans
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn charity secures funding to support veterans
A King’s Lynn-based charity, The Bridge for Heroes, has received a funding boost from the Veterans’ Foundation. The grant will allow the South Clough Lane organisation to expand its welfare services for serving personnel, veterans, and their families.
The charity aims to use the money to reduce isolation, anxiety, and stress within the Armed Forces community by providing accessible, person-centred support. CEO Helen Taylor says the funding will help the team reach more people in need. Anyone from the Armed Forces community seeking assistance or someone to talk to can contact the charity on 01553 760 230.

item.title: Wisbech youngster completes 93-mile charity walk
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech youngster completes 93-mile charity walk
An 11-year-old from Wisbech has raised over £3,200 for local charities after completing a 93-mile walk. Shyla Brown, a pupil at Peckover Primary School, walked from Silverstone race track to the Alan Hudson Centre in Wisbech over three days. Accompanied by Darren Barnard, she took more than 185,000 steps to honour the memory of Emma Barnard.
The funds raised will support the Alan Hudson Centre and Edith’s Purse, a charity providing aid to families in poverty. Shyla was greeted by the Mayor of Wisbech, Lucie Foice-Beard, as she completed the final leg of her journey on Sunday afternoon. Donations are still being accepted following the successful challenge.

item.description:

Cambridgeshire County Council considers school parking cameras
Cambridgeshire County Council is exploring the use of cameras outside schools to tackle illegal and dangerous parking. The authority’s highways and transport committee is reviewing a report on how camera technology could enforce traffic rules and support ‘school streets’ schemes, which restrict vehicle access during drop-off and pick-up times.
While councillors have welcomed the proposal, committee chair Alex Beckett noted that volunteers remain vital to the success of these zones. However, officials acknowledged that cameras may be necessary in areas where volunteers have faced harassment. Any implementation of these measures will require further assessment before receiving final approval.

item.title: King’s Lynn coffee shop reopens drive-thru following ram raid
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn coffee shop reopens drive-thru following ram raid
The Costa Coffee branch at St Nicholas Retail Park in King’s Lynn has reopened for drive-thru and delivery customers following a ram raid last week. The store on Edward Benefer Way was forced to close after a stolen car was driven into the building at 2:51am last Thursday. The incident caused significant damage to the main entrance, which has now been boarded up.
While the drive-thru lane is operational, the shop remains closed to walk-in customers. Norfolk Police confirmed that the stolen vehicle used in the raid has been recovered, though no arrests have been made at this stage. It is not yet known when the premises will fully reopen for sit-in service.

item.title: Drainage works to cause disruption on A149 near King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Drainage works to cause disruption on A149 near King’s Lynn
Drivers in the King’s Lynn area should prepare for delays starting September 21. Norfolk County Council is beginning a six-week project to upgrade drainage systems along the A149 Queen Elizabeth Way.
To allow for the work, two-way traffic lights will be in operation overnight between 7pm and 6am, Monday to Friday. Additionally, a reduced speed limit of 30mph and 40mph will be enforced around the clock across a 1.2-kilometre stretch. The project, which costs £105,000, will focus on the verge on the east side of the carriageway, beginning 280 metres north-east of the Gaywood River bridge. Motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly while these essential improvements are carried out.

A 37-year-old man from Gaywood has been found guilty of sexual assault. Sean Flanagan, of Bagge Road, appeared at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court yesterday for a summary trial. He was convicted of touching a woman aged 16 or over without her consent during an incident on November 18, 2025.

item.title: Future of key services at Queen Elizabeth Hospital under discussion
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Future of key services at Queen Elizabeth Hospital under discussion
Senior leaders at the Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group are discussing the potential closure of accident and emergency, intensive care, and maternity units at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. The group is developing a long-term strategy for the county’s hospitals, though they insist no final decisions have been made.
Officials state that any changes would require clinical evidence and formal public consultation. While the group maintains that urgent and emergency care will remain available at the site, this could involve scaled-down services. Local MPs have expressed differing views on the proposals, with calls for urgent reassurance regarding the hospital's future status. The facility is currently part of a planned 1.4 billion pound rebuild project.

We are taking a trip down memory lane to September 2013, when pupils at Gaywood Community Primary School in King’s Lynn began their autumn term with a historical twist. To encourage curiosity and engagement from the very first day, staff decorated classrooms and introduced themed costumes for the students.
Year Four children embraced the new school year by dressing in Tudor attire. Headteacher Paul Shanks explained that the initiative was designed to provide a memorable start to the term, prompting students to ask questions and immerse themselves in their learning immediately. item.title: Hospital team to tackle 180-mile challenge for new scanner
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Hospital team to tackle 180-mile challenge for new scanner
A spinal surgery team from Norfolk and Norwich University Hospitals is preparing for a six-day fundraising event to purchase a new EOS imaging system. Starting on Friday, September 4, the "Spineathlon 2026" will see the team kayak, walk, and cycle 180 miles across the region. Their route includes stops in Holkham, Hunstanton, and King’s Lynn. The appeal aims to raise the remaining funds for the £841,000 scanner, which provides accurate spinal images for children with scoliosis while reducing radiation exposure by 80 percent. So far, £660,000 has been collected through donations. The team will conclude their journey by cycling from the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn back to Norwich.

Concerns raised over potential service changes at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
Politicians in West Norfolk have expressed alarm following reports that the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn could face a downgrade. Discussions are reportedly underway regarding the potential closure of the hospital’s Accident and Emergency, intensive care, and maternity units as part of a long-term strategy.
Local councillors and campaigners have voiced strong opposition, warning that such moves would force patients to travel long distances for emergency care. However, the Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group states that no decisions have been made. Chief executive Professor Lesley Dwyer confirmed that clinical experts are developing a long-term strategy, but stressed that the hospital will continue to provide 24-hour urgent and emergency care for the local community.

The Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has issued an apology after a 79-year-old patient from Tilney St Lawrence reported feeling "frightened and unheard" during her stay last week. Jill Dewsbury, who was admitted with hip pain, claimed she was moved to a ward she believed was for dementia patients, leading her to accuse the hospital of ageist treatment.
The hospital’s chief nurse, Dawn Collins, has apologised for the distress caused. The trust clarified that the West Dereham ward is not a dementia unit, but cares for older adults with various medical needs. The hospital confirmed it is now reviewing the formal complaint submitted by Mrs Dewsbury.

West Norfolk Council defends swimming pool planning costs
West Norfolk Council is considering spending over £845,000 on the planning stages for new swimming facilities at Lynnsport in King’s Lynn. Council leader Alistair Beales has defended the expenditure as proportionate, citing the high costs of planning in a flood zone and rising construction prices. The proposed project aims to replace the existing St James Swimming Pool, which is currently safe but described as deteriorating.
The Corporate Projects Panel has recommended that the cabinet approve the funding at their next meeting on September 8. However, the council has declined to provide a public breakdown of the costs or reveal the price of extending the life of the current facility. There is no guarantee the new pool will be built.

A lifelong King’s Lynn Town supporter has fulfilled a final wish to watch his team play. Forty-three-year-old James Mason, who is battling a terminal illness, attended Monday’s National League North match against Scarborough Athletic at The Walks.
Club officials and local supporters helped arrange the visit, which included a presentation of a signed shirt and match ball from players Aaron Jones and Tom Dickens. Mr Mason, who has followed the Linnets since his teenage years, was accompanied by family and friends. The family expressed their gratitude to the club, the hospice charity Tapping House, and Clenchwarton Cabs for providing the transport necessary to make the day possible.

item.title: Police appeal for information on wanted man Liam Clarke
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Police appeal for information on wanted man Liam Clarke
Norfolk Police are searching for 47-year-old Liam Clarke, who is also known as Liam Cook. Officers are looking for him after he failed to attend a scheduled hearing at Norwich Magistrates’ Court. Mr. Clarke is described as five feet nine inches tall with a thin build, short brown hair, and blue eyes. He has known connections to King’s Lynn, Swaffham, and Wisbech.
Anyone with information regarding his current whereabouts is urged to contact the police via their website or by calling the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111. Please quote reference number 35/11070/26 when providing any details.

West Norfolk modellers raise over £2,300 for King’s Lynn Night Shelter
Members of the West Norfolk International Plastic Modellers’ Society have donated more than £2,300 to the King’s Lynn Night Shelter. The funds were raised during the club’s annual model show held at the Littleport Leisure Centre in June, which attracted 19 traders and over 200 members of the public.
The charity donation was presented to shelter representatives this past Wednesday. The club, which meets at the William Burt Social Club in West Winch, chooses a local charity to support each year. This latest contribution will assist the shelter, which does not receive government funding, in its ongoing work supporting the homeless across the region.

item.title: Queen Elizabeth Hospital addresses service closure concerns
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Queen Elizabeth Hospital addresses service closure concerns
The Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has issued a statement regarding the future of its services following reports of potential unit closures. The hospital trust confirms that no decisions have been made regarding the future of its Accident and Emergency, intensive care, or maternity departments.
Officials state they are currently exploring long-term clinical strategies for the Norfolk and Waveney area, but have no preferred options at this stage. The trust says any future proposals for significant service changes would require robust clinical evidence, as well as formal staff and public consultation. The hospital is currently working to address operational challenges as part of a long-term plan for healthcare across the region.
